info.name: QuickTweets — Verification (M1–M9)
info.description:
Manual verification of the Media subsystem and core flows.

IMPORTANT: Reference Coordination (the media_references ledger), TweetMedia rows, and MediaObject internals are NOT exposed by any API. This collection drives state; the DB checkpoints in verification-runbook.md verify coordination in pgAdmin. Run phase by phase, pausing at each checkpoint.

Auth: the access token is captured from the body into {{accessTokenA/B}} and sent as Bearer. The refresh + qt_session cookies are handled by Postman's cookie jar automatically. Because two users share one cookie jar on localhost, always authorize with the per-user Bearer token, never the cookie.

item.name: 09 · Username rename (WI-F)
item.description: Editable username with History + Reservation + Redirect. Self-isolated: Setup mints TWO fresh, uniquely-named users (a renamer + a bystander) so it never mutates verify_alice/verify_bob and stays re-runnable (each run's former handles are reserved indefinitely). Scenarios map 1:1 to USR-01…USR-10 in verification-scenarios.md and prove the three guarantees: G1 the session is id-based (the same Bearer minted BEFORE the rename still works and returns the new handle — no logout/refresh); G2 a former handle never 404s (301 on the profile URL, transparent resolution on the follow locator); G3 the rename reuses the SAME username validation as register. DB proof: Checkpoint H (username_aliases) in the runbook. Run top-to-bottom.

request.description: Pre-request mints unique handles for this run (rnOldUsername/rnNewUsername/rnBystander) so former-handle reservations from earlier runs never collide. This request registers the RENAMER as {{rnOldUsername}}; run S2 next for the bystander.

request.description:
Send this eleven times. Attempts 1-10 answer 400; the 11th answers 429 with type "rate_limit" — the per-IP limiter, distinct from CHV-03's per-address cooldown.

REQUIRES the restart CHV-12 performs. Six confirmations are already spent by CHV-04, 05, 06, 08 and CHV-10's two, so against a budget of ten the limiter would otherwise engage on this scenario's FIFTH attempt, not its eleventh. The restart clears the in-memory counter. Skipping CHV-12 breaks this scenario's arithmetic.

It then blocks confirmations for fifteen minutes, which is why nothing may follow it.

item.name: 11 · Password reset (PWR)
item.description:
Password reset — recovery for an account whose password its owner no longer has. Unauthenticated throughout: the actor is whoever holds the code.

**Setup precondition.** The server must run with `MAIL_MODE=capture`, which writes each message to `.mail-capture/` (relative to the API process's working directory). Without it the code is unobtainable and PWR-07 onward cannot run.

**And the migrations must be applied** — `password_reset_challenges`, `password_reset_sessions` and `mail_send_attempts`. The position lives in the second, and a missing one fails the folder at PWR-00. Every send passes through the mail mechanism's abuse controls, which fail closed when their state cannot be read.

**Self-isolated.** The folder mints its own account per run (`{{pwrUsername}}`), so it never disturbs the fixtures. Paste the captured code into `{{pwrCode}}` before PWR-07.

PWR-14 is a runbook step rather than a request: it needs a restart with a short `RESET_CODE_TTL_MS` and a shorter `RESET_RESEND_COOLDOWN_MS`, and a wait, neither of which a collection can carry.

**The position, and the key that addresses it.** Since ADR 0017 the reader's step is a server record addressed by an `HttpOnly` cookie, so `apply` carries only `{ newPassword }` and the runner must keep the cookie jar. Under Newman the run is necessarily split around the manual code paste, so the first leg needs `--export-cookie-jar` and the second `--cookie-jar`; without them PWR-07 onward fail on a position that is not there.

**Three subfolders, because the folder cannot run in one pass.** The break between 11.1 and 11.2 is the manual code paste; the break before 11.3 is a restart. Both were always constraints — they are now structure, so `--folder` addresses each leg directly instead of a runner having to know where to stop.

item.name: 12 · Comment thread
item.description:
The thread's two levels, its cursor pages, its refusals and its cascade (#799). Self-isolated: it mints its own account with a per-run handle and its own posts, and is non-destructive. Scenarios CMT-T01…CMT-T17 and Checkpoint K.

12.1 runs from the command line (npm run verify:thread) because every guarantee in it is visible in a body. 12.2's API half runs there too, but the ledger half cannot: whether a removed reply's media reference ended is invisible to every endpoint by design, so Checkpoint K is read in pgAdmin.

13 · Comment likes
item.description:
Likes on a comment and on a reply, the idempotence that replaced the toggle, and what a guest reads (#805). Self-isolated: its own account with a per-run handle, its own post and comments, non-destructive. Scenarios CML-01…CML-12.

It runs whole from the command line (npm run verify:likes) and needs no pgAdmin. That is the difference from folder 12: a like holds no media reference, so nothing about it is invisible to the API — the body tells the whole story, count and state alike.

request.description: Self-isolated: a per-run handle, so the folder collides with no other run.
